title: Seat a platform on three kinematic datums
context: Instrument carriers use a cup and groove and flat locating mount to return to a repeatable supported position without rocking. All three ball feet must be seated after the robot releases the carrier.
setup: Use the official bimanual YAM station with table top z 747.5 mm. x increases away from the arm bases and y increases toward the left arm. All heights below are above that table. The rigid grey base is 180 by 180 by 8 mm centred at x 260 mm and y 0. Its top is 8 mm high. The square cup centre is x 210 mm and y plus 50 mm. Its 40 by 40 by 2 mm floor spans heights 8 to 10 mm. Four triangular prism walls rise at 45 degrees from the cup centre at height 10 mm to the outer edges at height 30 mm. Each wall has 20 mm horizontal run and 20 mm rise and 40 mm span. The V groove centre is x 310 mm and y plus 50 mm. Its axis runs along x. Its 50 by 40 by 2 mm floor spans heights 8 to 10 mm. Two 50 mm long triangular prism faces run along x and rise at 45 degrees from the centre line at height 10 mm to y offsets plus and minus 20 mm at height 30 mm. The flat datum is 50 by 50 mm centred at x 260 mm and y minus 50 mm. Its bottom is 8 mm high and its top is 14.1421356 mm high. All datums are fixed rigid metal solids. The blue rigid metal plate is 160 by 150 by 12 mm and has mass 200 g. It starts level with zero yaw and centre x 100 mm and y 0 and height 28 mm. Three 20 mm diameter metal ball feet have centres 18 mm below the plate centre. Their plate-frame x and y offsets in mm are minus 50 and plus 50 for the cup foot then plus 50 and plus 50 for the groove foot then 0 and minus 50 for the flat foot. At the target all ball centres are 24.1421356 mm high and the plate centre is 42.1421356 mm high. Two polymer grip blocks 28 by 28 by 24 mm sit on metal stems 14 by 14 by 64 mm. Their centres are at plate offsets x 0 and y plus and minus 85 mm and z plus 65 mm. No front or rear naming convention is used. Exact primitive vertices and body masses are in scene_inventory.json.
scoring: Use the final score. A datum moving more than 2 mm or the plate passing more than 8 mm below the table or a nonfinite observed pose latches score zero. A datum contact is present when a native contact pair between that datum and the plate has separation at most 0.20 mm. In a physical replica a 0.20 mm feeler blade must not pass between the intended ball and its mating support without lifting the plate. This is a contact clearance test and not a force measurement. Cone and groove and flat are tested separately. Target plate centre is x 260 mm and y 0 and height 42.1421356 mm. Aligned means each x and y error below 3 mm and height error below 3 mm and tilt and absolute yaw below 3 degrees. With alignment and all three datum contacts and plate linear speed below 8 mm per second and angular speed below 0.1 radian per second the score is 0.75. Every finger joint open beyond 35 mm from its centre with no robot contact within 1 mm of the plate gives 0.9 until the full conditions hold continuously for one second and then 1.0. Interruptions restart that hold. Otherwise any datum contact with plate tilt below 10 degrees gives 0.5. Otherwise a plate whose lowest point is more than 15 mm above the table gives 0.25. All other outcomes score zero. Contacts and score history are sampled at 20 Hz. No force threshold is used.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the level plate back at x 0.10 and y 0 with centre 28 mm above the table. Leave the datums in their fixed positions. Recreate the scene and clear score history. Use the two handles for physical manipulation.
fidelity: Native rigid sphere to convex cup and groove and flat contacts. The scorer checks each support contact separation to 0.20 mm gauge resolution and robot release rather than contact force. No surface compliance or manufacturing variation is simulated. Datums are fixed. Plate motion is passive and is never assigned by a task callback.
instruction: Seat the blue platform on its matching cup and groove and flat datums. Leave all three ball feet seated and both hands clear. The fixture is unpowered.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds of control time.
scores: Dream 1 run: 0.0 in 2400 steps. Scripted demo: 1.0 in 262 steps.
